entries.title: Meta fined $567m in largest child safety ruling against social media giant
entries.snippet: The ruling is in addition to $375m in fines Meta was already ordered to pay in the case, for a total of $942m.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign defence pact
entries.snippet: Pakistan says an attack on any of the three will amount to an attack against all, amid conflict in the Middle East.

entries.title: Trump again tries to limit US birthright citizenship with new executive orders
entries.snippet: The executive orders ban birth tourism and expand the existing definition of people whose children are not eligible for US birthright citizenship.

entries.title: Australian aviation crew carries out daring midwinter Antarctica rescue
entries.snippet: Team evacuated a patient from McMurdo Station after landing plane in total darkness and temperature of -43°C.

entries.title: US strikes $1.2bn deal to pay German firm to halt offshore wind projects
entries.snippet: The RWE payout is the latest in a string of deals cancelling wind energy projects, a power source long derided by Trump.

entries.title: Trump denies US weapons shortage and says information 'leakers' being 'hunted down'
entries.snippet: While precise data is classified, publicly available information suggests the US has used up many difficult-to-manufacture weapons.

entries.title: A new youth agitation grips an Indian state after 'cockroach' protests
entries.snippet: Weeks after the CJP protests shook Delhi, a new youth-led movement over jobs and recruitment is gathering force in Jharkhand.

entries.title: Thousands of migrants still in Ceuta after border crisis, local leader says
entries.snippet: The Spanish territory's mayor-president also says 100 deaths occurred as a result of 78,000 migrants crossing from neighbouring Morocco.

entries.title: South Korea space agency shares Moon images after SpaceX rocket debris crash
entries.snippet: Seoul's lunar orbiter captured images of the Moon before and after part of SpaceX's rocket hit its surface on Wednesday.

entries.title: Two people convicted in relation to death of French streamer
entries.snippet: Raphaël Graven, 46, died in August 2025, with his death live broadcast on the streaming platform Kick.

entries.title: Israel charges settler over killing of Palestinian involved in Oscar-winning West Bank film
entries.snippet: Yinon Levy is charged with reckless manslaughter over the July 2025 shooting of Odeh Hathaleen.

entries.title: Doge overstated claims to have saved Americans $110bn, watchdog finds
entries.snippet: A review of the body formerly charged with reducing government spending has found several issues with its calculations.

entries.snippet: The BBC has seen evidence from previous cases that Russian-linked proxies not only handled drones and explosives, but also delivered them to Germany.

entries.title: Sudan's invisible children - born in war with no legal identity
entries.snippet: Babies born as a result of rape are often unable to get a birth certificate, meaning a life-time of problems.

entries.snippet: Cortis's plea has drawn mixed reactions in a fandom that's obsessed with capturing every moment.

entries.title: India is a nation of walkers - but its cities forgot them
entries.snippet: India's top court has put the spotlight on unsafe footpaths and the country's forgotten pedestrians.

entries.title: Does Africa still back Infantino as Fifa president?
entries.snippet: The African confederation has yet to take an official stance, but where do the key African footballing nations stand on the Infantino saga?

entries.title: Livestreamer's murder raises questions over relations between Mexico's creators and cartels
entries.snippet: The murder of content creator César Gastélum on Tuesday raises questions about why influencers are coming under attack.

entries.title: In Odesa, no-one is safe from Russia's new Black Sea strikes
entries.snippet: Blackened ships and smashed docks mark Russia's recent surge of attacks on Ukraine's coastline.

entries.title: Banned from football at home, Afghan women's team reunite 8,000 miles away
entries.snippet: Women in the team, which is recognised by Fifa, say football has given them freedom and independence.

entries.title: Employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs in a sign of a wilting labor market
entries.snippet: U.S. employers cut 23,000 jobs in July, and job gains for the two previous months were weaker than initially reported, according to a report Friday from the Labor Department.

entries.title: A new vaccine could vanquish a major cause of deadly diarrheal disease
entries.snippet: Over 1 million people a year die from diarrheal disease. Nearly half are kids under age 5. A new vaccine in trials offers great hope.

entries.title: Trump targets birthright citizenship. And, Iran aims to ban U.S. from Strait of Hormuz
entries.snippet: President Trump says he has signed two new orders targeting birthright citizenship. And, Iran is aiming to ban U.S. ships from the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: Kalshi and Polymarket bets on clinical trials criticized as 'ghastly'
entries.snippet: Researchers warn betting on clinical trials could incentivize insider trading and interfere with drug development. But Kalshi and Polymarket say they provide valuable information to patients.

entries.title: Everyone's talking about hormone therapy for menopause. Should I be on it?
entries.snippet: For years, doctors advised against hormone therapy for women in the menopausal transition. Now everyone's talking about how great it is. Is it really a wonder drug that women should all be on?

entries.title: Who or what is 'taking a step back from visibility'? The quiz knows
entries.snippet: Plus, if you know what "TMZ" stands for, you'll get at least on question right this week!

entries.title: Amid cost of living stress, many parents are supporting children well into adulthood
entries.snippet: Polls show most Americans think young adults today have it harder financially than past generations. A majority of parents help their grown children with expenses, even if it hurts their own finances.

entries.title: Besieged Sudanese city faces relentless drone strikes and risk of mass atrocities, U.N. warns
entries.snippet: Hundreds of thousands of civilians in el-Obeid are being battered by relentless drone strikes and face critical water shortages and a worsening cholera outbreak, while women and girls are reporting high rates of sexual violence.

entries.title: When tragedy strikes, America's wildland firefighters ask, was it 'somebody that we loved?'
entries.snippet: Deaths and close calls while fighting wildfires have strained an already on-edge workforce. They've also raised questions about policies and priorities amid an intense wildfire season.

entries.title: Morning news brief
entries.snippet: Trump issues new orders to limit birthright citizenship, Iran shares details of an agreement with Oman to reopen Strait of Hormuz, Trump under pressure to find a breakthrough with Iran.

entries.title: U.S. employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs amid strain from the Iran war, unemployment dips to 4.1%
entries.snippet: U.S. employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs last month, and Labor Department revisions shaved 103,000 jobs off payrolls in May and June. The unemployment rate dipped to 4.1% only because Americans left the job market.

entries.title: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567 million over mental health harms to kids online
entries.snippet: Judge Bryan Biedscheid said in a ruling late Thursday that the bulk of the money — $420 million — will be used for treatment services for young people. The rest will go toward awareness and prevention, screening services and other costs over the next five years.

entries.title: The major changes Head Start faces under Trump proposal

entries.title: Greece deploys satellite detection system to combat deadly wildfires
entries.snippet: New satellites are being used in Greece to help fight another vicious wildfire season there. The technology is helping crews spot and contain fires. Special correspondent Malcolm Brabant reports from the town of Mati, near Athens.

entries.snippet: How did American English become so distinctly American? On her "In Pursuit of Happiness" podcast, Judy Woodruff sat down with linguists Anne Curzan and Valerie Fridland. They look at how Americans from the very beginning reshaped the English language by changing pronunciations an

entries.title: After Michigan, Democrats' next battleground over the party's future shifts to Wisconsin
entries.snippet: In a year where voters upset with the Democratic Party mainstream have propelled outsider candidates to victory across the country, this candidate is hoping to buck the trend in Wisconsin.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump signs executive orders imposing new limits on birthright citizenship

entries.title: Uganda approves sending troops to Gaza for international force proposed by Trump's Board of Peace
entries.snippet: The successful motion, brought by the defense minister, is Uganda's first public indication of its willingness to join the International Stabilization Force for Gaza. Morocco also has pledged troops for the mission.

entries.title: Man charged with arson in Spokane told police he planned to spark wildfire for weeks
entries.snippet: A Spokane County detective who interviewed the man accused of starting one of the city's wildfires said the man confessed, described his planning process and explained how he created a device to ignite the blaze.

entries.title: Why was Fauci held in contempt for pleading the 5th, and what happens next?
entries.snippet: A Senate committee voted along party lines to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress on Thursday, a week after the former top health official and scientist refused to answer questions in a hearing about the COVID-19 pandemic.

entries.title: How Abdul El-Sayed rose from political oblivion to progressive breakthrough in Michigan
entries.snippet: El-Sayed, 41, has never held elected office and entered the race seven years after losing Michigan's Democratic gubernatorial primary by more than 20 percentage points.

entries.title: Poll shows how extreme heat is changing Americans' lives
entries.snippet: A new AP-NORC poll finds that Americans are increasingly noticing the impact of extreme heat on their lives, and they say much of that shift is happening in the West and Midwest.

entries.title: WATCH: Scientists release most detailed sun images ever
entries.snippet: Researchers were able to peek at its scorching surface with the help of the National Science Foundation's Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope, located on the island of Maui in Hawaii.

entries.title: Trump pushes ahead on false claims Reflecting Pool was vandalized
entries.snippet: Jeanine Pirro this week found out there's a trade-off between loyalty to President Donald Trump and being loyal to reality.

entries.title: GOP Rep. Max Miller resists pressure to drop reelection bid as party anxiety grows over abuse claims
entries.snippet: Miller is facing a congressional ethics investigation related to domestic abuse allegations leveled against him by his ex-wife but is insisting he won't withdraw.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing seeks legitimacy in Thailand
entries.snippet: Bangkok rolled out the red carpet for the Myanmar leader, but experts say the former junta chief still faces major obstacles in his bid for regional acceptance.

entries.title: Germany: Far-right AfD extends its lead in nationwide polls
entries.snippet: In the latest Sunday poll, the AfD continues to pull ahead. And more and more people are against excluding the right-wing populists from decision-making, at least on a case-by-case basis.

entries.title: Middle East: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defense deal
entries.snippet: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defense deal. According to the agreement, an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be regarded as an attack against all of them. Follow DW for the latest.

entries.title: Germany news: Exports and factory data lift economic outlook
entries.snippet: German exports hit a record high in June, while industrial production rose for a third month in a row. Meanwhile, more than 1,000 pigs have died in a fire at a farm in Bavaria. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
entries.snippet: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.

entries.title: Is it really the hottest day ever?
entries.snippet: Every time a new heat record is broken, skepticism follows. How do scientists know a day or a summer was really the hottest on record or that a heat wave was historic? DW has the answers.

entries.title: India news: CJP announces plan for nationwide campaign
entries.snippet: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has unveiled the agenda for its "Kya Bolti Public" campaign, which will start in September. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Thailand: Several killed in school shooting north of Bangkok
entries.snippet: The shooting incident took place at the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in ​the ‌Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi, just north of the capital city of Bangkok. Several people were killed in the attack.

entries.title: US judge orders Meta to pay $567 million over harm to children
entries.snippet: A New Mexico judge ruled Meta created a "public nuisance" that harmed children's mental health, ordering the company to pay over half a billion dollars in damages and overhaul safety features on Facebook and Instagram.

entries.title: Argentina: Milei's property bill triggers protests, anger
entries.snippet: Police clashed with protesters in Buenos Aires after thousands rallied against President Javier Milei's private property bill. The government had already dropped a provision on foreigners buying land in Argentina.

entries.title: Trump signs new orders restricting birthright citizenship
entries.snippet: The US president's move comes just two months after the Supreme Court ruled that his first executive order on citizenship was unconstitutional.

entries.title: Ebola: Africa CDC plans to use vaccine for different strain as outbreak spreads
entries.snippet: The head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control pledged to deploy a vaccine for a previous Ebola strain in the current DRC outbreak, with test cases indicating a potentially live-saving level of protection.

entries.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
entries.snippet: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

entries.title: Ceuta leader says 100 migrants died in border rush
entries.snippet: With over 3,000 migrants still in Ceuta after rushing the border last week, Ceuta leader Juan Jesus Vivas warns the situation in the Spanish exclave is "unsustainable." Hundreds of those migrants are minors.

entries.title: Germany news: Officials deny reports of drone near munitions-laden plane
entries.snippet: Officials in Germany have rejected reports that an explosive-laden drone found at Leipzig airport was next to a plane filled with weapons destined for Ukraine. Federal prosecutors have taken over the case.

entries.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
entries.snippet: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.

entries.title: Can UN chief's initiative kickstart resolution for Cyprus?
entries.snippet: UN chief Antonio Guterres considers a resolution to the Cyprus issue to be vital for regional stability and has initiated a new diplomatic effort. What are the prospects for its success?

entries.title: Why Iran is sending mixed signals on talks
entries.snippet: Trump says talks with Iran are underway. Tehran says it is discussing the Strait of Hormuz with Oman, not Washington. Analysts say the gap reflects competing political pressures.

entries.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
entries.snippet: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.
